text.en:
The drum was beaten in Meenapuram and everyone gathered under the banyan tree.
The panchayat president read out the money spent on the new well. An old woman asked, "Why was the road not repaired?"
The president noted her question and promised an answer.

The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all the adult voters of a village. Every adult man and woman who has a vote is a member and can speak.
In the meeting the panchayat tells the people how money was spent and what work is planned. People can ask questions and suggest what the village needs, such as water, roads or a school.
The Gram Sabha makes the panchayat answerable to the people. It is a true example of people taking part in governing themselves.

problem.en: Why should women also attend the Gram Sabha?

text.en: Every adult voter is a member, including women.
Women know village needs such as water and health.
So their presence makes decisions fairer.

prompt.en: A friend says only the panchayat president takes decisions in a village. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: The Gram Sabha, with all adult voters, can ask questions and give suggestions.
The panchayat must answer to it.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking one person governs the village.

points.en: The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adult voters of a village.
It discusses money, plans and needs.
